parties.respondent_defendant: Sarita & minor daughter — wife and child

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2007. The respondent claimed maintenance pendente lite, but the appellant argued that the marriage was void as the respondent's earlier husband had not been divorced.

legal_principles.principle: Maintenance under Section 125, Cr.P.C. cannot be denied where there is some evidence on which conclusion for grant of maintenance could be reached.
legal_principles.held: It was held that order passed under Section 488 is a summary order which does not finally determine the rights and obligations of the parties;
cited_cases: S.Sethurathinam Pillai v. Barbara @ Dolly Sethurathinam, (1971) 3 SCC 923

legal_principles.principle: The term 'wife' occurring in Section 125, Cr.P.C. is to be given a very wide interpretation.
legal_principles.held: A broad and expansive interpretation should be given to the term 'wife' to include even those cases where a man and woman have been living together as husband and wife for reasonably long period of time;
cited_cases: Chanmuniya vs. Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha & Anr., IX(2012) SLT 534=I (2013) DMC 131 (SC)=(2011) 1 SCC 141

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order for maintenance was upheld.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
